# Downloading Files Generated by MCP Servers

An assistant with MCP servers can produce files for the user, such as an Excel report, a CSV export, a JSON dump, a ZIP archive or a PDF. AI/Run CodeMie stores each delivered file in the conversation and shows it in the reply as a **Download** chip with the file name and a type badge. The same files are listed in **Browse files** for the conversation.

Image files work as before: they are shown inline.

## How Files Reach the Chat

A file reaches the chat in one of three ways:

| Source                                                                                                                                 | Configuration needed                               | Result in chat                   |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------- |
| The MCP server returns the file content in the tool result (an embedded resource), for example the Filesystem server `read_media_file` | None                                               | Download chip                    |
| A stdio MCP server writes the file to disk, and the model names it in the `codemie_export_files` argument                              | Opt the server in with `CODEMIE_EXPORT_FILES=true` | Download chip                    |
| A stdio MCP server returns a `file:///` link to the file (a `resource_link`)                                                           | Opt the server in with `CODEMIE_EXPORT_FILES=true` | Download chip                    |
| The MCP server returns an `http://` or `https://` link                                                                                 | None                                               | Plain clickable link, not stored |

When a file cannot be delivered, the reply says so in plain text, for example `` `report.xlsx` stays on the MCP server and was not delivered ``. No link to a local path such as `filesystem:/home/...` is shown.

## What the User Sees

- Each file appears as a **Download** chip with its name. Hovering over the type badge shows the MIME type.
- Clicking the chip downloads the file under its original name and with the correct extension.
- If the same name is delivered twice in one reply, the second file is named `name (2).ext`.
- All delivered files are listed in **Browse files** for the conversation, under `artifacts/<turn-id>/<name>`.
- Recipients of a [shared conversation](../../../assistants/share-assistant-chat-with-other-users.md) can download the files as well.

## Files Returned by the Server

When an MCP server returns the file bytes in its tool result, the file becomes a Download chip with no extra configuration. The [Filesystem MCP server](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/servers/tree/main/src/filesystem) does this with its `read_media_file` tool.

:::note
Use `@modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem` version 2026.7.10 or later. Earlier versions return non-image files in a shape that fails MCP validation, so no file is delivered.
:::

To make the assistant use this path on the first request, add a rule to the assistant instructions, for example:

```text
To give the user a generated file, call read_media_file on it. Never print a local file path.
```

## Exporting Files Written by a stdio Server

A stdio MCP server, such as a shell server, often writes a file to disk and returns only a text message. To deliver such files, opt the server in to file export.

### Step 1: Opt the Server In

Add `CODEMIE_EXPORT_FILES` with the value `true` to the `env` block of the server in the [JSON configuration](./adding-an-mcp-server.md#add-mcp-server-with-json-method-manual-setup). The values `1`, `yes` and `on` are accepted too.

Shell server example:

```json
{
  "command": "uvx",
  "args": ["cli-mcp-server"],
  "env": {
    "ALLOWED_DIR": "/home/codemie",
    "UV_CONSTRAINT": "/etc/uv-constraints.txt",
    "CODEMIE_EXPORT_FILES": "true"
  }
}
```

Filesystem server example:

```json
{
  "command": "npx",
  "args": ["-y", "@modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem", "/home/codemie"],
  "env": {
    "CODEMIE_EXPORT_FILES": "true"
  }
}
```

:::warning
Set `CODEMIE_EXPORT_FILES` in the server configuration itself. A value supplied through environment variables of an integration or user credentials is ignored.
:::

`UV_CONSTRAINT` is required for servers started with `uvx`. The child process does not inherit the image-wide value, and without it `uvx` resolves a version of `mcp` that `cli-mcp-server` cannot start with.

The setting applies only to stdio servers. HTTP and SSE servers never export files. The key is removed before the server process starts, so the server itself never receives it.

### Step 2: Tell the Assistant Where to Write Files

On an opted-in server, every tool gets an optional `codemie_export_files` argument. The model lists in it the paths of the files the user should receive. The argument description tells the model to write such files under `/home/codemie/codemie_export`.

Repeat this in the assistant instructions to make delivery reliable:

```text
When you create files for the user, write them under /home/codemie/codemie_export
and list the same paths in codemie_export_files.
```

### Step 3: Wait for the Tool Cache

The new argument appears after the toolkit cache of the CodeMie API expires, which takes up to 10 minutes after the server configuration is saved. Test the assistant after that.

### How the Export Folder Works

`/home/codemie/codemie_export` is an alias. For each tool call, MCP Connect maps it to a folder that belongs to the current user and conversation:

```text
/home/codemie/u-<user hash>/c-<conversation hash>/
```

The folder is created before the tool runs. As a result:

- Two users who ask for a file with the same name get their own files, never each other's.
- Two conversations of the same user are kept apart too.
- Each person who runs a shared or global assistant gets a separate folder.
- A file from an earlier turn of the same conversation can be delivered by naming it again in a later call.

Only regular files inside the conversation folder are exported. Paths outside the folder, symlinks, `..` segments, hidden paths such as `.ssh`, directories, missing files and empty files are refused. Every refused file is listed with its reason in the tool result, so the model can write the file to the right place and try again. When the tool call itself fails, nothing is exported.

### Links to Files

An opted-in stdio server can also return a `file:///` link instead of the file content. MCP Connect reads the linked file and replaces the link with the file itself. The same folder rules and limits apply. A refused link is replaced by a short note with the reason.

## Limits

The administrator of MCP Connect can change these limits. See [MCP Connect File Export](../../../../admin/configuration/codemie/api-configuration.md#mcp-connect-file-export).

| Limit                                    | Default |
| ---------------------------------------- | ------- |
| Size of one exported file                | 50 MiB  |
| Total size of exported files in one call | 50 MiB  |
| Number of exported files in one call     | 20      |
| Number of `file:///` links read per call | 50      |

## Known Limitations

- The file size is not shown on the Download chip.
- Files from MCP tool nodes in workflows are not delivered yet.
- Files from MCP tools that run through CodeMie Plugins are not delivered yet.
- A resource that carries only a `uri` and a link with a scheme other than `file`, `http` or `https` are reported as not delivered.
- Opting in is not access control. A shell or Filesystem server that can read `/home/codemie` can still read other users' folders on purpose. Opt in only servers whose access to `/home/codemie` is acceptable and whose output is trusted to name files.
- When the model does not list its files in `codemie_export_files`, no chip appears. Clear assistant instructions reduce such misses.
- Exporting the same file in two separate calls produces two chips.
